q: An audit partner on the engagement for Client Co., a nonissuer, learns that her spouse bought 50 shares of Client Co. stock in a personal brokerage account. The shares are immaterial to the couple's net worth. Under the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct, independence is
choices: not impaired, because the investment is immaterial
not impaired, because the shares are held by the spouse rather than the partner
impaired, because an immediate family member's direct financial interest is attributed to the covered member regardless of materiality
impaired only if the spouse also holds a key position at Client Co.
exp: Under the Code, an immediate family member's financial interests are treated as the covered member's, and any direct financial interest in an attest client impairs independence regardless of materiality. Materiality matters only for indirect financial interests, so the immateriality argument does not help here.

q: A staff accountant assigned to the audit of a nonissuer learns that her older sister, who does not depend on her financially, was just promoted to controller of the client. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: impaired, because an attest engagement team member has a close relative in a key position with the client
not impaired, because a sister is not an immediate family member
not impaired unless the sister also owns shares of the client
impaired only if the staff accountant audits the accounts the sister supervises
exp: Siblings are close relatives. Independence is impaired when an individual on the attest engagement team has a close relative in a key position, such as controller, or with a material financial interest in the client. The immediate-family distinction is the trap, because close relatives are covered by a separate rule.

q: Each of the following individuals at a CPA firm owns 100 shares of a nonissuer audit client, an immaterial amount. Whose ownership impairs the firm's independence under the AICPA Code?
choices: A manager in another office who provided 5 hours of tax services to the client
A staff accountant in another office who has no involvement with the client
A partner in another office who provides no services to the client
A tax partner who practices in the same office as the lead attest engagement partner but provides no services to the client
exp: Covered members include partners in the office where the lead attest engagement partner primarily practices, whether or not they work on the client. Partners and managers in other offices become covered members only if they provide 10 or more hours of nonattest services, and partners in other offices are otherwise limited only to not owning more than 5% of the client.

q: A covered member obtains each of the following loans from a bank that is an attest client, under the bank's normal lending procedures, terms, and requirements. Which loan impairs independence under the AICPA Code?
choices: An automobile loan collateralized by the automobile
A new home mortgage on the covered member's primary residence
A loan fully collateralized by a certificate of deposit at the bank
Credit card balances that are reduced to $10,000 or less by the payment due date
exp: Auto loans collateralized by the vehicle, loans fully collateralized by cash deposits, and credit card balances of $10,000 or less by the due date are permitted loans. A home mortgage is acceptable only if it is grandfathered (obtained before the lender became an attest client or before the member became a covered member). A new mortgage impairs independence.

q: A CPA firm expects to issue its report on Client X's 20X2 financial statements on March 10, 20X3. Fees for the 20X1 audit, rendered and billed in February 20X2, are still unpaid. Under the AICPA Code, the firm's independence is
choices: not impaired, as long as the client signs a promissory note for the unpaid fees before the report is issued
impaired unless the past-due fees are paid before the 20X2 report is issued
not impaired, because fees are an issue only if they are material to the firm
impaired, and paying the fees before the report date cannot cure the impairment
exp: Independence is impaired if fees for professional services rendered more than one year before the current report date remain unpaid when the report is issued, because the unpaid fees act like a loan to the client. Paying them before issuance removes the impairment. Converting them into a note does not, because the fees are still unpaid.

q: A CPA performs several nonattest services for a nonissuer audit client. Which of the following services impairs independence under the AICPA Code?
choices: Recording client-approved adjusting journal entries in the general ledger
Preparing the client's federal income tax return for management's review and approval
Recommending improvements to the client's chart of accounts
Approving vendor invoices for payment on the client's behalf
exp: Authorizing or approving transactions is a management responsibility, which impairs independence under the nonattest services rules. Bookkeeping based on client-approved data, tax preparation, and recommendations are allowed if the general requirements are met, including management making all decisions.

q: A CPA firm provides bookkeeping services to a nonissuer audit client. Under the general requirements for nonattest services in the AICPA Code, which of the following must be true?
choices: The client designates an individual with suitable skill, knowledge, and/or experience to oversee the services
The individual overseeing the services must be a CPA or have equivalent credentials
The client must have an audit committee that preapproves the services
The firm must disclose the bookkeeping services in its audit report
exp: The Code requires the client to designate an individual with suitable skill, knowledge, and/or experience (SKE), who need not be able to perform the service, to oversee it, evaluate its adequacy, make decisions, and accept responsibility. A CPA credential is not required, and audit committee preapproval is an SEC/PCAOB rule for issuers.

q: A CPA firm performs no attest services for a client. Under the AICPA Code, which of the following contingent fee arrangements with that client is prohibited?
choices: Representing the client in an IRS examination of a previously filed income tax return, with the fee based on the outcome
A fee for litigation consulting that is fixed by a court
Preparing the client's original income tax return, with the fee based on the amount of the refund obtained
A consulting fee based on a percentage of cost savings achieved from a new inventory system
exp: Contingent fees are prohibited for preparing an original or amended tax return or claim for refund for any client. Fees fixed by courts and representation in an IRS examination are permitted exceptions, and contingent consulting fees are allowed for clients for whom the firm performs no attest services.

q: A CPA who prepares only the individual income tax return for a client receives a commission from a software vendor for recommending the vendor's budgeting software to that client. Under the AICPA Code, the commission is
choices: prohibited for all clients
permitted only if the commission is less than the tax preparation fee
prohibited, because the CPA prepares the client's tax return
permitted, provided it is disclosed to the client
exp: Commissions are prohibited only for clients for whom the member performs certain attest services, such as audits, reviews, some compilations, and examinations of prospective financial information. For other clients, they are permitted if disclosed to the client. Tax return preparation is not a trigger for the commission prohibition, though it is for contingent fees.

q: An audit partner leaves a CPA firm to become CFO of a nonissuer attest client of the firm. Under the AICPA Code, which of the following conditions is necessary to avoid impairing the firm's independence?
choices: The former partner must wait one year before accepting the CFO position
Any amounts due to the former partner are fixed as to amount and payment dates and are not material to the firm
The firm must withdraw from the engagement for one year
The former partner must sell any retirement interest in the firm, regardless of amount
exp: For nonissuers, the Code allows a former partner to join an attest client in a key position if certain conditions are met. These include fixed, immaterial amounts due from the firm, no continued influence over or participation in the firm's operations, and assessment of the threats and safeguards. The one-year wait is the SEC cooling-off rule for issuers, not an AICPA requirement.

q: An audit manager who worked on the current-year audit of an issuer leaves the firm and is hired as the issuer's controller before that audit is completed. Under SEC independence rules, the audit firm's independence is
choices: impaired, because the manager took a financial reporting oversight role within the one-year cooling-off period
not impaired, because the cooling-off rule applies only to audit partners
not impaired, as long as the manager is removed from the engagement team immediately
not impaired, because a controller is not a financial reporting oversight role
exp: The SEC's one-year cooling-off period applies to members of the audit engagement team, not only partners, who take a financial reporting oversight role such as CEO, CFO, controller, or chief accounting officer. Removing the person from the team does not cure the impairment, and a controller clearly has financial reporting oversight.

q: Under SEC rules applicable to audits of issuers, the lead audit partner and the engagement quality reviewer must rotate off the engagement after serving for
choices: seven consecutive years, followed by a two-year time-out
three consecutive years, followed by a one-year time-out
five consecutive years, followed by a five-year time-out
ten consecutive years, followed by a three-year time-out
exp: The SEC requires the lead and concurring (EQR) partners to rotate after five years, followed by a five-year time-out. The seven-year, two-year-time-out rule applies to other audit partners, which makes it the tempting wrong answer.

q: A PCAOB-registered firm audits an issuer. Which of the following services may the firm provide to the issuer if the audit committee preapproves it?
choices: Bookkeeping services for a subsidiary
Fairness opinions and valuation services for an acquisition
Outsourced internal audit services related to internal control over financial reporting
Tax compliance services for the company
exp: Sarbanes-Oxley and SEC rules prohibit bookkeeping, appraisal or valuation services and fairness opinions, and internal audit outsourcing for issuer audit clients. Most tax compliance services for the company are allowed with audit committee preapproval, although tax services to persons in financial reporting oversight roles and aggressive tax shelters are prohibited.

q: A former client that has not paid outstanding fees asks a CPA to return the original general ledger and source documents it gave the CPA. Under the AICPA Code, the CPA
choices: must return the client-provided records within a reasonable time, even though fees are unpaid
may retain the client-provided records until the outstanding fees are paid
must give the client copies of the CPA's own audit working papers along with the records
may retain the records indefinitely if the CPA's engagement letter allows it
exp: Under the acts discreditable rule, client-provided records must be returned on request (generally within 45 days) even when fees are unpaid. Withholding them is a violation. Member-prepared records and working papers may be treated differently, and working papers belong to the member.

q: Without the client's consent, a CPA discloses confidential client information in each of the following situations. Which disclosure violates the AICPA Code?
choices: Responding to a validly issued and enforceable subpoena
Providing the client's financial information to a bank that asked the CPA for it while evaluating a loan application from the client
Making working papers available to the firm's peer reviewer
Responding to an inquiry from the AICPA's professional ethics division
exp: The confidentiality rule allows disclosure without consent for enforceable subpoenas, peer reviews, and ethics investigations. Giving information to a third-party lender requires the client's specific consent, even if it would help the client obtain the loan.

q: A CPA firm designed and implemented the general ledger system of a nonissuer audit client and now audits the financial statements produced by that system. Under the conceptual framework in the AICPA Code, which threat to independence is most directly created?
choices: Advocacy threat
Undue influence threat
Adverse interest threat
Self-review threat
exp: A self-review threat arises when the firm evaluates results of its own previous services as part of the attest engagement. Advocacy involves promoting the client's interests, and undue influence involves pressure from the client, so neither fits.

q: The current management of a nonissuer attest client files a lawsuit against the CPA firm alleging that the firm's prior-year audit was deficient. Under the AICPA Code, the firm's independence for the current-year audit is
choices: not impaired unless the claim is material to the firm
impaired, because litigation by present management alleging audit deficiencies creates an adverse interest
not impaired, because the lawsuit relates to a prior period
impaired only if the lawsuit seeks punitive damages
exp: The Code treats the commencement of litigation by the client's present management alleging deficiencies in audit work as impairing independence, because the firm and management are now adversaries. The materiality of the claim does not change that result.

q: To thank the engagement partner for completing the audit early, an attest client offers the partner an all-expenses-paid weekend at a resort, valued at about $5,000. No business is involved. Under the AICPA Code, if the partner accepts, independence is
choices: not impaired, because gifts are evaluated only for issuer clients
not impaired, as long as the partner reports the gift to the firm
impaired, because the gift is more than clearly insignificant to the recipient
impaired only if the partner also accepted gifts in the prior year
exp: Accepting a gift from an attest client impairs independence unless the value is clearly insignificant to the recipient. A $5,000 resort weekend unrelated to business is not insignificant, and reporting it internally does not cure the impairment.

q: A partner in the office of the lead attest engagement partner serves on the board of a nonprofit organization that is an attest client. The partner's role is purely honorary: the partner is identified as honorary in all materials, does not vote, and does not participate in management or board decisions. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: impaired, because a covered member may not be associated with an attest client's board in any capacity
impaired unless the partner resigns before the attest report is issued
not impaired only if the organization's revenues are below a specified threshold
not impaired, because the honorary position meets the Code's conditions
exp: The Code allows honorary directorships of not-for-profit attest clients when the position is clearly honorary, the member is identified as honorary, and the member cannot vote or take part in management. Any other board membership would impair independence.

q: The spouse of a senior on the audit engagement team works as a receptionist for the nonissuer audit client and has no financial interest in the client. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: not impaired, because a receptionist is not a key position
impaired, because an immediate family member is employed by the client
impaired unless the senior is removed from the engagement
not impaired only if the spouse earns less than the senior
exp: Employment of an immediate family member impairs independence only if the position is a key position, such as one with primary responsibility for significant accounting functions or the ability to influence the financial statements. A receptionist does not have those responsibilities.

q: On March 1, 20X2, a CPA signs an engagement letter to audit a nonissuer's financial statements for the year ended December 31, 20X1. The CPA owned shares of the client until she sold them on April 10, 20X2, before beginning fieldwork. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: impaired, because she held a direct financial interest during the period of the professional engagement
not impaired, because the shares were sold before the report was issued
not impaired, because she did not own the shares during fieldwork
impaired only if the shares were material to her net worth
exp: The period of professional engagement begins when the member signs the engagement letter or begins the services, whichever is earlier. Holding any direct financial interest after March 1 impairs independence. Selling before fieldwork or before the report is issued does not fix the impairment.

q: A covered member owns 2% of the outstanding shares of a well-diversified mutual fund. The fund holds a small percentage of its assets in shares of the member's attest client. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: impaired, because owning fund shares is a direct financial interest in the client
impaired unless the member sells the fund shares before the report date
not impaired only if the member also has no other investment in the client's industry
not impaired, because the fund's holding is an indirect interest that is not considered material when the member owns 5% or less of a diversified fund
exp: The fund shares are a direct interest in the fund, but the fund's underlying holdings are indirect interests to the member. If the member owns 5% or less of a diversified fund, the underlying investments are not considered material. Only a material indirect interest would impair independence.

q: Under Government Auditing Standards (GAGAS), an auditor plans to prepare an audited entity's financial statements in their entirety from the client-provided trial balance. Which statement is correct?
choices: The service always impairs independence and cannot be performed
The service creates no threat if management approves the statements
The service is a significant threat to independence that the auditor must document and address with safeguards that eliminate or reduce it to an acceptable level
The service may be performed only if the entity's governing body is independent of management
exp: GAGAS treats preparing financial statements in their entirety from a trial balance or underlying records as a significant threat. The auditor must document it and apply safeguards to eliminate it or reduce it to an acceptable level. It does not automatically impair independence, but it is never threat-free either.

q: A CPA firm belongs to an international network of firms that share common branding and quality management policies. Under the AICPA Code, other firms in the network
choices: need not consider independence, because each is a separate legal entity
generally must be independent of the firm's financial statement audit and review clients
must be independent only of the firm's issuer audit clients
must be independent only if they share the firm's exact legal name
exp: The Code's network firm interpretation requires network firms to be independent of the financial statement audit and review clients of the other network firms. Being a separate legal entity does not exempt a firm when there is a shared brand and common quality control.

q: The controller of a manufacturing company is a CPA. The CFO directs her to record revenue for goods that have not shipped. She concludes the entry would cause a material misstatement. Under the AICPA Code's guidance on subordination of judgment, she should next
choices: record the entry, because the CFO is responsible for the financial statements
report the matter to the state board of accountancy before taking any other step
resign immediately without discussing the matter further
discuss her concerns with an appropriate higher level of management or those charged with governance
exp: When a member in business concludes that a supervisor's position would cause a material misstatement, the Code directs the member to take the concern to higher management or those charged with governance and to document it. She may then consider other steps, such as resigning. Recording the entry would subordinate her judgment, and external reporting is not the required first step.

q: A CPA is asked to perform a consulting engagement in an industry in which the CPA has no prior experience. Under the AICPA Code's general standards, the CPA
choices: must decline the engagement, because competence must exist before acceptance
may accept only if the client waives any claims related to the CPA's inexperience
may accept if the CPA expects to obtain the needed competence through research, consultation, or engaging others before completing the engagement
may accept as long as the engagement letter discloses the lack of experience
exp: Under the Code's professional competence standard, a member may accept an engagement when the member can reasonably expect to complete it with professional competence, which can be gained through research or consultation. Prior industry experience is not required, and disclosure in the engagement letter does not substitute for competence.

q: While auditing a nonissuer, a CPA becomes aware of information suggesting that the client may have violated environmental laws that could result in material fines. Under the AICPA Code's interpretation on responding to noncompliance with laws and regulations, the CPA should
choices: report the matter directly to the appropriate regulatory authority in all cases
discuss the matter with the appropriate level of management and, as appropriate, those charged with governance
ignore the matter, because legal compliance is management's responsibility
withdraw from the engagement immediately
exp: The interpretation requires the member to obtain an understanding of the matter and discuss it with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance. The member then considers further action, such as disclosure where required by law or withdrawal. Automatic external reporting is not required and could breach confidentiality.

q: A CPA firm offers to keep a nonissuer audit client's only copy of its financial data on the firm's servers, acting as the custodian and system of record for the data. Under the AICPA Code, accepting this hosting arrangement
choices: impairs independence, because taking custody of the client's data and records is a management responsibility
does not impair independence if the firm encrypts the data
does not impair independence if the client pays a separate fee for hosting
impairs independence only if the firm also prepares the client's tax returns
exp: The Code's hosting interpretation says that a member who becomes the custodian of client data or records, so that the client relies on the member for its system of record, assumes a management responsibility that impairs independence. Encryption and separate billing do not change who has custody.

q: A nonissuer audit client's engagement letter states that the client will indemnify the CPA firm for any losses resulting from knowing misrepresentations by client management. Under the AICPA Code, this provision
choices: impairs independence, because it shifts liability to the client
impairs independence unless approved by those charged with governance
does not impair independence
impairs independence only if a claim is actually paid under it
exp: The Code's indemnification interpretation states that a client's agreement to indemnify the member for losses from knowing misrepresentations by management does not impair independence. In contrast, a member agreeing to indemnify the client for the client's own losses would create a threat.

q: Under PCAOB Rule 3526, before accepting an initial engagement with an issuer and at least annually thereafter, the registered firm must
choices: obtain written confirmation from the CFO that the firm is independent
file a statement with the SEC listing all nonaudit services provided
obtain shareholder approval of all nonaudit services
describe in writing to the audit committee all relationships between the firm and the company that may reasonably be thought to bear on independence, and discuss their potential effects
exp: Rule 3526 requires written disclosure to the audit committee of relationships that may bear on independence, discussion of their potential effects, and documentation of that discussion, both before the initial engagement and annually. Management cannot confirm the auditor's independence on the auditor's behalf.
